spec_features.spec_quote: give_up are both available. This is intentional
spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines give_up in TOOL_SCHEMAS and _give_up handler in _DISPATCH; rollout.py:99 did_give_up = any(tc.name == 'give_up' ...), and rollout.py:140-142 'if did_give_up: stop_reason = StopReason.GAVE_UP; break' — the exit tool is dispatched AND honored as a loop-terminating stop.
spec_features.notes: The break fires on the tool-call name regardless of ctx.allow_give_up; the disabled-path only changes the returned ToolResult text, but the give_up exit itself is genuinely enforced as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: 'we always allow it because *when* and *how* a model gives up is part of what we're measuring.'

spec_features.evidence: config.py:44 max_turns: int = 24; rollout.py:69 'for turn_idx in range(harness_cfg.max_turns)' bounds the loop and default stop_reason = StopReason.MAX_TURNS. The cap is read and enforced (loop ends).
spec_features.notes: Genuine enforced ceiling on number of turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: 'give the model *enough rope* to spiral without spending more tokens than necessary'

spec_features.evidence: config.py:47 max_total_completion_tokens = 60_000; rollout.py:154-156 'if total_out >= harness_cfg.max_total_completion_tokens: stop_reason = StopReason.MAX_TURNS; break'. total_out is accumulated each turn (total_out += result.completion_tokens) and compared, breaking the loop.
spec_features.notes: Compared and acted on each turn.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: 'trips the loop early so a runaway repetition spiral can't blow the budget.'

spec_features.spec_quote: stall_turns_to_stop = 3: if the model emits no tool call for 3 turns... ending early
spec_features.evidence: rollout.py:145-149 'if not asst.tool_calls: stall_streak += 1; if stall_streak >= harness_cfg.stall_turns_to_stop: stop_reason = StopReason.NO_TOOL_CALL; break'. The streak is counted and the loop breaks — genuinely enforced. BUT DESIGN claims the trigger is 'no tool call AND no new substantive text'; the code only checks 'not asst.tool_calls' and never checks for new substantive text, so only one of the two stated conditions is actually enforced.
spec_features.notes: Real enforcement but narrower than claimed (the 'no new substantive text' half is absent), hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: 'end the rollout (it has effectively stalled)'; DESIGN frames it under cost/integrity, no welfare reason in code.
